title: Model Question Paper 2
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 100 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper

Section A: questions 1–20 are MCQs (1 mark each). Section B: questions 21–35 have two parts of 1 mark each.
Section C: 2-mark answers in 30–50 words, 3-mark answers in 50–80 words, 5-mark answers in 80–120 words.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match, one word or identify).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Today, because of ________, the whole world has become a big market. (b) Paying taxes to the government honestly and regularly is a responsibility of business towards the ________.
Usha works in an oil refinery and Kiran in her family textile business. Name the type of industry in each case.
questions.answer:
(a) Oil refinery — manufacturing (processing) industry.
(b) Textile industry — manufacturing industry.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Industry is concerned with ________ of goods. (b) The medium which moves men and materials from one place to another is called ________.
Write True (T) or False (F): (a) The liability of a sole proprietor is limited. (b) The principle of one person one vote applies to sole proprietorship.
questions.answer:
(a) False — it is unlimited.
(b) False — it applies to cooperative societies.

questions.q: Give one-word answers: (a) Can minors be members of a Hindu Undivided Family business? (b) How many successive generations can be members of an HUF business?
questions.answer:
(a) Yes — membership is by birth.
(b) Three.

questions.q: Mrs. Reeta is afraid that if her business assets fall short, her personal assets may be used to pay the debts. (a) Which form of organisation should she choose? (b) Why?
questions.answer:
(a) A joint stock company.
(b) Its shareholders have limited liability — they lose at most the value of their shares; personal assets are safe.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) To complete the process of communication there should be at least ________ persons. (b) ________ communication includes sounds, words, language and speech.
Write True (T) or False (F): (a) Overdraft can be given on a current account. (b) For a bank, deposits are an asset.
questions.answer:
(a) True
(b) False — deposits are a liability (money owed to depositors).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The consideration of insurance is known as ________. (b) The principle of utmost good faith is based on ________ between insurer and insured.

questions.answer:
(a) W — a wholesaler deals in one line of goods.

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) Advertising is a powerful communication force and an important activity of the promotion mix. (b) Salesmen get no help from advertising while selling.
questions.answer:
(a) True
(b) False — advertising gives customers product knowledge in advance, which helps salesmen.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is a partnership? Explain in your own words.
questions.answer: A partnership is an agreement between two or more persons to carry on a lawful business together and share its profits and losses. Each partner contributes capital or skill, takes part in management and has unlimited liability; the partners together are called a firm.

questions.q: 'Members may come and members may go, but the company continues to exist.' Identify and explain this feature of a joint stock company.
questions.answer: Perpetual succession. A company is a separate legal entity created by law, so its life is not affected by the death, insolvency, retirement or transfer of shares of any member. It ends only when it is wound up by law.

questions.q: What is the difference between a debit card and a credit card?
questions.answer: A debit card pays from the holder's own bank balance, which is reduced at once. A credit card lets the holder buy on credit up to a limit and pay the bank later; interest is charged if not paid within the credit period.

questions.q: Distinguish between a whole-life policy and an endowment policy.
questions.answer:
Whole-life: runs for the insured's whole life; premium is paid throughout; the sum is paid to the heirs only after death.
Endowment: runs for a fixed period or up to a certain age; the sum is paid at maturity, or to the heirs if the insured dies earlier.

questions.q: What is meant by the right to safety? Explain with an example.
questions.answer: The right to be protected against goods and services that are hazardous to life and health. Example: if a gas cylinder supplied leaks and causes a fire, the supplier is liable to pay compensation.

questions.q: Explain briefly feasibility study and identifying entrepreneurial opportunities as functions of an entrepreneur.
questions.answer:
Identifying opportunities: sensing changing human needs (food, fashion, education) faster than others and finding a business in them — the first function.
Feasibility study: studying whether the proposed product will succeed — market demand, inputs, costs, sources and problems — and preparing a business plan or project report.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Differentiate between economic and non-economic activities on the basis of purpose, outcome and expectation.
questions.answer:
Purpose: economic activities aim to earn money; non-economic activities aim at satisfaction (love, social or religious feeling).
Outcome: economic activities produce income and wealth; non-economic activities give personal satisfaction.
Expectation: in economic activities a monetary return is expected; in non-economic activities no return is expected.

questions.q: Why do members of a cooperative society not work with full zeal? Explain along with other limitations.
questions.answer:
Members get only a limited dividend on capital and no extra reward for extra effort, and office-bearers are often honorary — so there is little personal motivation.
Other limitations: limited capital; inefficient management; conflicts among members; excessive government control; lack of secrecy.

questions.q: Ajay's business suffers from changes in fashion and prices and tough competition; Vijay's from dishonesty of employees and customers and from strikes. Name the types of business risk.
questions.answer:
Ajay — economic-cause risks (changes in fashion, prices, competition; speculative risks).
Vijay — human-cause risks (dishonesty of employees and customers, strikes and lockouts).

questions.q: State any three differences between wholesalers and retailers.
questions.answer:
(1) Buying: wholesalers buy from producers in bulk; retailers buy from wholesalers in small quantities.
(2) Variety: wholesalers deal in a limited line; retailers in a wide range.
(3) Purpose of sale: wholesalers sell for resale; retailers sell for consumption.

questions.q: Explain the right to be heard and the right to seek redressal.
questions.answer:
Right to be heard: consumers' interests must receive due consideration — they are consulted in government policy, business listens to their views, and they are heard in consumer courts.
Right to seek redressal: consumers can get replacement, refund or compensation for defective goods, deficient services and unfair practices, through the seller or the consumer courts.

questions.q: An air purifier advertised as removing 100% germs did not work for Priya; testing showed it had no such capacity. What malpractice is involved and which rights can she exercise?
questions.answer:
Malpractice: misleading advertisement (false claim of quality).
Rights: right to be informed (she was given false information); right to seek redressal — she can file a complaint for refund or replacement and compensation in the District Commission; right to be heard.

sections.title: Long answer questions, including case-based questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain primary, genetic and extractive industries with suitable examples of each.
questions.answer:
Primary industry: produces goods with the help of nature, needing little human effort — agriculture, farming, forestry, fishing, horticulture.
Genetic industry: reproduces and multiplies certain species of plants and animals with the aim of selling them for profit — plant nurseries, cattle breeding, poultry farms, fish hatcheries.
Extractive industry: draws out goods from the soil, air or water; its products are usually raw materials for manufacturing and construction — mining of coal and iron ore, drilling of oil, extraction of timber and rubber from forests.

questions.q: Explain any five barriers to effective communication.
questions.answer:
(1) Badly expressed message — poor choice of words or language causes misunderstanding.
(2) Screening or filtering — the message gets distorted as it passes through levels.
(3) Inattention — people do not read or listen carefully.
(4) Unclarified assumptions — sender and receiver assume different things.
(5) Resistance to change — people ignore messages that disturb routine.
(6) Mutual distrust; status and position; complex organisation structure.

questions.q: State any six differences between wholesalers and retailers.
questions.answer:
(1) Quantity — bulk vs small.
(2) Buy from — producers vs wholesalers.
(3) Variety — limited line vs wide range.
(4) Capital — more vs less.
(5) Sale — for resale vs for consumption.
(6) Contact with consumers — none vs direct.
(7) Decoration of shop — little vs much.

questions.q: Enlist any five areas of self-employment and give one example of each.
questions.answer:
(1) Small-scale retail business — a grocery shop.
(2) Services based on individual skills — a tailoring or hair-dressing shop.
(3) Professions — a doctor's private clinic.
(4) Small-scale farming — dairy or poultry.
(5) Village and cottage industries — handloom weaving.
(6) Arts and crafts — goldsmith, carpenter, potter.
